title: 空管还在用软盘？
title_en: Air Traffic Control Runs on Floppies?

segments.zh: America's air traffic control
still runs partly on floppy disks.
The FAA says floppies carry weather and other key information
segments.en: 美国联邦航空局说，四百多个空管设施

segments.zh: at more than four hundred facilities.
segments.en: 靠软盘传天气等关键信息。

segments.zh: This week it promised
to phase them out by the end of twenty twenty eight.
Floppies mostly vanished more than twenty five years ago,
segments.en: 软盘早在二十五年前就基本没人用了，

segments.zh: and have not been mass produced since twenty eleven.
Reuters reports that some replacement parts
segments.en: 路透社报道，有些替换零件，

segments.zh: were bought on eBay.
Today's brain teaser: how does a thin piece of plastic
segments.en: 今天的烧脑问题：一片薄薄的塑料，

segments.zh: remember anything at all?
Meet our hero, Floppy:
one point four four megabytes of pure attitude.
segments.en: 一点四四兆字节的倔脾气。

segments.zh: One point four four megabytes
is roughly one phone photo.
segments.en: 大约就是一张手机照片。

segments.zh: Your phone might hold two hundred fifty six gigabytes.
segments.en: 你的手机也许有二百五十六 G，

segments.zh: By our math, that is about one hundred seventy thousand Floppies.
segments.en: 我们算了下，相当于十七万张软盘。

segments.zh: Twist one: inside, there is no paper and no ink.
segments.en: 反转一：里面没有纸，也没有墨，

segments.zh: Just a thin disk coated with a kind of rust.
segments.en: 只有一张涂着“铁锈”的薄圆片。

segments.zh: That rust is packed with tiny magnets,
segments.en: 这层铁锈里全是小磁铁，

segments.zh: far too small to see.
Each tiny patch points one way or the other.
segments.en: 每一小块，磁铁要么朝这边，要么朝那边：

segments.zh: One way means one, the other way means zero.
Like a stadium crowd
flipping cards up or down to make a picture.
segments.en: 举牌子朝上或朝下，拼出一幅画。

segments.zh: Spin the disk, and a little head
flips the magnets as they pass. That is writing.
segments.en: 就把经过的小磁铁一块块翻过来，这就是写。

segments.zh: Reading is the reverse:
segments.en: 读正好反过来：小磁铁经过线圈，

segments.zh: passing magnets nudge a tiny current through a coil.
Twist two: magnets are stubborn.
Leave them alone, and they stay put.
segments.en: 你不碰它，它就一直这么指着。

segments.zh: Some rocks have kept their magnetism
for millions of years.
So why replace floppies?
Twist three: the disk is fine; the world around it is not.
segments.en: 反转三：盘没坏，是它周围的世界变了。

segments.zh: Drives wear out. Heads get dirty.
segments.en: 驱动器会磨损，磁头会脏，

segments.zh: And nobody makes new ones.
Bring a strong magnet close,
and the weather data can get scrambled.
Plastic ages,
and that rusty coating can flake off.
And speed: by our estimate,
reading a whole disk takes about a minute.
segments.en: 读完一整张大约要一分钟。

segments.zh: The FAA's chief put it this way:
every facility is a silo.
When data cannot flow over a network,
someone has to carry it.
The plan: one new display system
segments.en: 新计划：一套新的显示系统，

segments.zh: replaces four systems from the nineteen eighties.
segments.en: 一口气替换四套八十年代的老系统。

segments.zh: Congress approved twelve and a half billion dollars last year,
segments.en: 国会去年批了一百二十五亿美元，

segments.zh: and the transportation secretary wants thirty billion more.
segments.en: 交通部长还想再要三百亿。

segments.zh: Paper flight strips are retiring too:
segments.en: 纸质的飞行进程单也要退休：

segments.zh: twenty seven big airports have already dropped them.
segments.en: 二十七个大机场已经不用了。

segments.zh: Why so slow?
You cannot switch off the sky to upgrade it.
It is like swapping a plane's engine
while it is still flying.
Fine print: old does not mean unsafe.
segments.en: 友情提示：老，不等于不安全。

segments.zh: These machines have run for decades.
But hunting for spare parts on eBay
segments.en: 但从 eBay 上淘零件，

segments.zh: is not a long term plan.
And here is the irony:
big data centers still archive on magnetic tape.
segments.en: 大型数据中心今天还在用磁带存档。

segments.zh: Same trick as Floppy:
tiny magnets, pointing one way or the other.
So how does plastic remember?
segments.en: 所以塑料凭什么能记住东西？

segments.zh: It does not. Millions of tiny magnets do.
segments.en: 它记不住，是上千万个小磁铁在记。

segments.zh: Floppy is not retiring because it forgot.
segments.en: 小软退休，不是因为它忘了。

segments.zh: It is retiring because everyone forgot how to talk to it.
segments.en: 是因为大家都忘了怎么跟它说话。
